subject.title: [Feature]: Feishu Group Chat SubAgents for User-Specific Skills and Memory

question: Should OpenClaw add automatic Feishu group per-sender subagents with isolated skills/config/memory, or keep group behavior to session/thread routing plus explicit spawned subagents?
rationale: The request changes channel ownership, plugin APIs, security boundaries, persisted agent state, lifecycle policy, and user skill/config semantics, which cannot be selected safely by a narrow fix bot.

options.title: Design a Feishu plugin-owned group subagent contract
options.body: Specify lazy creation, cleanup/TTL, quotas, memory namespaces, permission boundaries, routing rules, and upgrade behavior before implementation.

options.title: Keep current scopes and explicit subagent sessions
options.body: Document groupSessionScope, DM dynamic agents, and sessions_spawn thread flows as the supported path while leaving automatic group subagents out of scope.

options.title: Split the umbrella into prerequisite issues
options.body: Track app/session identity, threading policy, and user skill preferences separately before deciding whether the full group-subagent feature should exist.

recommendation.title: Design a Feishu plugin-owned group subagent contract
recommendation.body: Specify lazy creation, cleanup/TTL, quotas, memory namespaces, permission boundaries, routing rules, and upgrade behavior before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-main history places this person on the central Feishu session, dynamic-agent, and subagent-hook implementation paths.
